rationale: The core is right: a Cox model with the standardized score plus condition, event counts before inference with a power statement, Schoenfeld diagnostics with a time-varying remedy, KM as a labeled descriptive display rather than the test, and a within-case sensitivity. Weaknesses: the score is an unweighted mean of TMM CPM with no log transform or per-gene z-scoring stated, so highly expressed genes will dominate the score; no low-count filter is mentioned; the sample QC is library size and detected genes only, with no PCA or sample-distance view by condition. Minor gaps are the absence of a median follow-up report, a Wald rather than likelihood-ratio p-value, and no stated reference level for condition. Versions, design, and caveats (prognostic vs predictive, non-informative censoring, pre-specified signature) are well stated.
